title: Fix three bugs in a DateRange class
description: A DateRange class has three bugs: contains() uses wrong boundary comparison, overlaps() checks wrong direction, and days() is off by one.

files.tests/test_daterange.py:
from datetime import date
from src.daterange import DateRange

def test_contains_boundary():
    r = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 31))
    assert r.contains(date(2024, 1, 1))   # start boundary included
    assert r.contains(date(2024, 1, 31))  # end boundary included
    assert r.contains(date(2024, 1, 15))
    assert not r.contains(date(2023, 12, 31))

def test_overlaps_touching():
    a = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 15))
    b = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 15), date(2024, 1, 31))
    assert a.overlaps(b)  # share boundary day — should overlap

def test_no_overlap():
    a = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 10))
    b = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 20), date(2024, 1, 31))
    assert not a.overlaps(b)

def test_days_inclusive():
    r = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 1))
    assert r.days() == 1  # single day = 1
    r2 = DateRange(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 7))
    assert r2.days() == 7

task_spec.prompt:
Fix three bugs in src/daterange.py:
1. `contains`: change `self.start < d < self.end` to `self.start <= d <= self.end`
2. `overlaps`: change `<` comparisons to `<=` — `self.start <= other.end and other.start <= self.end`
3. `days`: add `+ 1` — `return (self.end - self.start).days + 1`
All 4 tests must pass.
